topic: exp2_cat coverage-gap root cause and SP-side zero-prior fallback
trigger: User directive: identify what causes the exp2_cat coverage gap (run-log WARNING: exp2_cat_k_offspeed_diff / exp2_cat_xwoba_offspeed_diff at 57% measured vs 64% baseline) and remediate toward full coverage.

root_cause.method: Gap-row attribution over the full 7,382-game frame (scratch tune_exp2_coverage.py output, 2026-09-30 frame): every NaN in the served diffs decomposed to its missing formula input.
root_cause.finding: 100% of gap rows have at least one starter with ZERO prior tracked PAs of that pitch category this season (the season-to-date ASOF prior is legitimately NULL). Team-side category inputs are NaN in only 1.4% of gap rows (offspeed). Offspeed is worst because it is ~11% of league PA usage (fastball/breaking ~89%), so a starter much more often has no prior offspeed sample; 197 season-opening March games are structurally unfillable from personal history.
root_cause.old_behavior: Zero-prior SP cells shipped NaN and rode per-fold median imputation inside the members — fabricating 'league-average offspeed' for the matchup product on ~43% of offspeed rows. For the served LEVEL twins, imputation additionally asserted a usage the pitcher has never shown.

remediation.change: SP-side zero-prior cells collapse to no-edge (features.py, mirroring the 6b3b3e2 shrinkage philosophy): rate cells (sp_k_pct_cat / sp_xwoba_cat / sp_k_pct_fb_vs) fall back to the strictly-prior league rate for that date (SP deviation-from-league exactly 0 = no information); usage cells ship 0.0 (a KNOWN ZERO of tracked usage, per the user's reasoning). Team-side gaps still propagate NaN (never fabricate the opponent). Day-1 rows (no league prior anywhere) stay NaN via 0*NaN propagation — the only residual, 0.7% of rows.
remediation.tests: test_exp2_no_history_fallback.py (8 tests on the emitted SQL templates with in-memory DuckDB): league fallback, known-zero usage, personal cells untouched, day-1 NULL, strictly-prior semantics (own-game exclusion, LAG-shifted league publication), fbhand fallback, team-side propagation. Battery 191 passed.

gate.design: A/B on the production-identical exported frame (game_level_features.csv, 7,382 games, identical folds/seed/blend mechanics; scratch tune_exp2_gate.py): baseline = current NaN->imputation arithmetic; fallback = SP sources filled then all 24 exp2 columns recomputed via features.add_exp2_features (exactly what the next DuckDB build does). Both JSONs: mlb_exp2_fallback_gate_{baseline,fallback}_20261001.json.
gate.verdict: ADOPT — pooled logloss better (-1 bp), pooled AUC -3 bp (inside the documented +/-0.001 not-measurably-worse band, model_tuning_policy SS4), pooled ECE better (-10 bp); the recent-form seal window (the folds the blend actually earns from) improves on ALL FOUR metrics, ECE by -73 bp. Beyond the numbers, the old behavior was semantically wrong: median imputation asserted league-average offspeed ability from zero evidence. The 49-row residue is day-1-no-league-prior, not remediable without leaking.

scope_notes: Runs are multi-threaded (production is not thread-pinned): 1e-4-scale deltas carry thread noise; the verdict rests on the seal sign-consistency, the ECE improvements, and the coverage/semantics correction.
Served level twins now express the known-zero usage semantics (0.0 instead of imputed) — part of the same correction, covered by the same gate.
exp2_cat_platoon_k_fastball_diff gains the same fbhand fallback (94.7% -> ~100%).
